title: RO-MT084-RoleMigrationImporter

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the Role Migration Importer: a read-only ingester that turns the existing repo-gov role protocols into DRAFT Handshake Roles (hsk.handshake_role@1, MT-081). The eight source protocols Handshake Roles streamline (verified in wt-gov-kernel): .GOV/roles/orchestrator/ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/coder/CODER_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/wp_validator/WP_VALIDATOR_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/integration_validator/INTEGRATION_VALIDATOR_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/kernel_builder/KERNEL_BUILDER_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/classic_orchestrator/CLASSIC_ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/activation_manager/ACTIVATION_MANAGER_PROTOCOL.md, .GOV/roles/memory_manager/MEMORY_MANAGER_PROTOCOL.md. These protocols share a recognizable structure: role identity/definition sections, duty lists (HBR gate obligations, planning/claim/handoff duties), gates (proof gates, checklists, repomem/receipt gates), and forbidden actions (e.g. Orchestrator 'Does NOT create refinements/worktrees', 'Does NOT validate or approve', Coder role-chain 'never skip a role / never assume another role's responsibilities'). The importer extracts identity/duties/gates/forbidden-actions into a STREAMLINED overlay_prompt plus a tool_policy proposal. Imported roles are PROPOSALS: status=draft, provenance.source=imported — operator approval (activate transition, exercised via MT-085 GUI) is required before any imported role can be injected. The importer runs read-only against a CONFIGURABLE roles-source directory (portability: no hardcoded .GOV path, no hardcoded drive letters).

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/role_importer.rs (RoleImporter + protocol parser + streamliner + draft writer via HandshakeRoleStore), config key for the source directory, an import HTTP route or CLI entry (POST /api/roles/import) returning a typed import report, plus tests with vendored protocol fixtures. No .GOV writes ever.

DETAILED SPEC:
- Config: roles_import_source resolved from (in order) explicit request parameter, HANDSHAKE_ROLES_IMPORT_SOURCE env var, config file key. No default pointing into any repo; unset + no parameter = typed RoleImportError::SourceNotConfigured.
- pub struct RoleImporter { store: HandshakeRoleStore } with pub async fn import_dir(&self, source: &Path, options: ImportOptions) -> Result<ImportReport, RoleImportError>.
- Discovery: scan source dir for */[A-Z_]+_PROTOCOL.md (one level of role subdirs, matching the .GOV/roles layout); role id derived from the subdirectory name kebab-cased (orchestrator -> orchestrator, wp_validator -> wp-validator, etc.).
- Extraction per protocol (markdown heading-based, tolerant of missing sections):
  * identity: role-definition / role-ecosystem sections -> title + description + opening identity block of overlay_prompt.
  * duties: duty bullet lists (HBR gate obligations, claim/planning/handoff duties, closure discipline) -> condensed duty section.
  * gates: proof/handoff/checklist gate statements -> 'gates you must honor' section.
  * forbidden actions: 'Does NOT ...', 'never ...', 'Do not ...' normative bullets -> explicit forbidden-actions section.
- Streamlining rules (this is migration, not copying): drop repo-local mechanics that do not survive productization (script paths, .mjs helper invocations, .GOV file paths, Just recipes); keep behavioral duties, gates, and forbidden actions; cap streamlined overlay_prompt at the MT-082 overlay size budget; every dropped-section decision listed in the ImportReport so the operator can audit the streamlining.
- tool_policy proposal: conservative mapping from role nature (e.g. validator/orchestrator roles propose deny on file-edit tool classes; coder/builder roles propose allow) — explicitly marked proposal-quality in the report; operator edits via MT-085.
- provenance: { source: "imported", source_ref: "<relative protocol path>@sha256:<content hash>" }.
- Idempotency: re-import with unchanged source content is a no-op (dedupe by source content hash against existing versions' provenance); changed content creates a NEW draft version, never mutates an existing one.
- ImportReport (typed JSON): per-role { role_id, action: created|new_version|unchanged|skipped, source_ref, dropped_sections: [], warnings: [] }.
- Read-only guarantee: importer opens source files read-only and writes only to PostgreSQL via HandshakeRoleStore; no writes, renames, or lockfiles in the source tree.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Vendor two realistic fixture protocols (modeled on ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md and CODER_PROTOCOL.md structure: identity, duties, gates, forbidden actions) under the crate's test fixtures — tests never read .GOV/.
2. Implement source resolution + SourceNotConfigured typed error.
3. Implement discovery walk + role-id derivation (snake_case dir -> kebab-case id) with collision detection.
4. Implement heading/bullet extraction into the four buckets; missing bucket -> warning in report, not failure.
5. Implement streamlining rules + size cap + dropped-section accounting.
6. Implement tool_policy proposal mapping table.
7. Write drafts through HandshakeRoleStore.create_role/new_version with imported provenance; never call activate (compile-visible: importer has no activate path).
8. Implement content-hash idempotency + ImportReport assembly; wire the POST /api/roles/import route.
9. Tests: fixture import creates drafts with correct ids/provenance; re-import unchanged = no-op; changed fixture = new draft version; importer-never-activates negative test; read-only guarantee test (source dir mtimes/contents unchanged); SourceNotConfigured test; forbidden-actions extraction test against fixture bullets.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** except named IPC read surfaces
.GOV/** (role protocols are read-only source material; importer reads, never writes)
acceptance_criteria: Importer resolves its source directory from parameter/env/config only; unset source yields typed SourceNotConfigured, never a hardcoded .GOV or drive-letter default.
Importing the fixture set produces DRAFT roles with status=draft, provenance.source=imported, and source_ref carrying relative path + content sha256.
Extraction populates identity, duties, gates, and forbidden-actions sections of overlay_prompt from fixture protocols; missing sections produce report warnings, not failures.
Streamlining drops repo-local mechanics (script paths, .GOV references, Just recipes) and lists every dropped section in the ImportReport.
Re-import of unchanged sources is a no-op (action=unchanged); changed source creates a new draft version; no existing version row is ever mutated.
The importer has no code path to activate a role (negative test: after import, zero active roles exist that were not active before).
Source tree is untouched after import (read-only guarantee test).
Import runs against the real .GOV/roles/ protocols only in MT-087's round-trip proof; this MT's tests are fixture-hermetic.
expected_tests: fixture import -> draft roles with imported provenance
implementation_notes: Verified source inventory (wt-gov-kernel .GOV/roles/): orchestrator/ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md, coder/CODER_PROTOCOL.md, wp_validator/WP_VALIDATOR_PROTOCOL.md, integration_validator/INTEGRATION_VALIDATOR_PROTOCOL.md, kernel_builder/KERNEL_BUILDER_PROTOCOL.md, classic_orchestrator/CLASSIC_ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md, activation_manager/ACTIVATION_MANAGER_PROTOCOL.md, memory_manager/MEMORY_MANAGER_PROTOCOL.md. A ninth legacy dir (roles/validator/) exists; discovery handles it like any other but nothing special-cases it.

Protocol structure observed: markdown H1/H2 sections mixing role definition (e.g. 'Orchestrator Role Definition (ORCHESTRATOR_MANAGED)'), duty lists ('HBR Gate Obligations', claim/handoff duties), gates, and normative 'Does NOT' / 'never' bullets — the extractor keys on these patterns, not on exact section titles.
Imported overlays are proposals for the operator to review/edit/approve in MT-085; fidelity matters less than honest dropped-section accounting.

Portability [GLOBAL-PORTABILITY]: the same importer must later ingest role sources from OTHER projects built by Handshake — nothing may assume the Handshake repo layout beyond the subdir/*_PROTOCOL.md convention, and that convention is a documented default, overridable via ImportOptions glob.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend importer MT; the operator reviews/approves imported drafts through the MT-085 Role Manager GUI. ImportReport JSON + registry ledger events are the trace projection.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Import workflow is operator-facing only through the MT-085 GUI and the /api/roles/import route documented in the MT-085 manual entry (draft-review-approve walkthrough).

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.behavior: protocol import producing draft role versions + ImportReport
hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: internal_diagnostics/Palmistry not yet shipped in wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1; registry ledger events (MT-081) + ImportReport are the Tier-1 evidence surface.

risk_if_missed: The eight proven repo-gov role protocols never migrate into the product; Handshake Roles start empty, operators hand-author overlays from scratch, and the repo-gov-to-product streamlining (the stated purpose of Handshake Roles) has no mechanical path.

risks: RISK-1: Silent auto-activation — imported prompts going live without operator review would inject unreviewed, possibly repo-specific instructions into product sessions.
RISK-2: Lossy streamlining hides authority — dropping a forbidden-action or gate bullet without accounting turns a guarded role into an unguarded one, and nobody can tell what was lost.
RISK-3: Source-tree contamination — importer writes (lockfiles, normalized rewrites, temp files) into .GOV/ or another governance tree, corrupting read-only source material.
RISK-4: Duplicate-version churn — non-deterministic extraction (map ordering, whitespace) makes every re-import look 'changed', flooding the registry with junk draft versions.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): importer has no activate call path (compile-visible + negative test); drafts require the MT-081 explicit activate transition driven by the operator.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): every dropped section/bullet class is enumerated in ImportReport.dropped_sections; forbidden-action bullets are never eligible for dropping (test asserts fixture 'Does NOT' bullets survive).
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): read-only file access + post-import source-tree integrity test (contents and mtimes unchanged).
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): content-hash idempotency computed over raw source bytes (not extracted output); unchanged-source re-import proven no-op.

research_provenance.source: Directly inspected .GOV/roles/* in wt-gov-kernel: all eight named *_PROTOCOL.md files verified present; ORCHESTRATOR_PROTOCOL.md and CODER_PROTOCOL.md read for structure (role definition sections, HBR gate obligation duty lists, handoff/claim gates, 'Does NOT'/'never' forbidden-action bullets). Operator context: Handshake Roles = streamlined productized successors of these startup inject-prompts, for Handshake AND future projects built by Handshake; operator authors/approves, models consume. MT-081 registry is the write target.
corrections: Imported roles are proposals (draft + imported provenance), never directly injectable — approval is an operator act.
Configurable source directory, no hardcoded .GOV path: the importer must serve future Handshake-built projects, not just this repo [GLOBAL-PORTABILITY].
Streamlining is honest-lossy: repo mechanics dropped, behavioral duties/gates/forbidden actions kept, all drops accounted in the ImportReport.
